claim: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) represents only 10–15% of all breast cancer cases.
source: Despite representing only 10–15% of all breast cancer cases, it is associated with a greater risk of recurrence, metastasis, and resistance to chemotherapy, leading to a poorer prognosis than other types of breast cancer (Geyer et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Geyer et al., 2017

claim: TNBC is associated with a greater risk of recurrence, metastasis, and resistance to chemotherapy compared to other types of breast cancer.
source: Despite representing only 10–15% of all breast cancer cases, it is associated with a greater risk of recurrence, metastasis, and resistance to chemotherapy, leading to a poorer prognosis than other types of breast cancer (Geyer et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Geyer et al., 2017

claim: TNBC has a poorer prognosis than other types of breast cancer.
source: Despite representing only 10–15% of all breast cancer cases, it is associated with a greater risk of recurrence, metastasis, and resistance to chemotherapy, leading to a poorer prognosis than other types of breast cancer (Geyer et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Geyer et al., 2017

claim: Treatment approaches for TNBC include the use of EGFR inhibitors, PARP inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and anti-angiogenic therapies.
source: In the clinic, in addition to surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, treatment approaches for TNBC also include the use of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitors, poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and anti-angiogenic therapies (Zagami and Carey, 2022; Garcia et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Zagami and Carey, 2022; Garcia et al., 2020

claim: Cancer cells can increase the synthesis and secretion of VEGFA to stimulate tumor angiogenesis.
source: Cancer cells can increase the synthesis and secretion of the vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA), activate endothelial cells in neighboring blood vessels through paracrine pathways, and stimulate tumor angiogenesis (Detmar, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Detmar, 2000

claim: VEGFA activates endothelial cells in neighboring blood vessels through paracrine pathways.
source: Cancer cells can increase the synthesis and secretion of the vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA), activate endothelial cells in neighboring blood vessels through paracrine pathways, and stimulate tumor angiogenesis (Detmar, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Detmar, 2000

claim: STAMBPL1 belongs to the AMSH family and cleaves K63-linked polyubiquitin chains.
source: The deubiquitinase STAMBPL1 (also known as AMSH-LP) belongs to the AMSH family and cleaves K63-linked polyubiquitin chains (Sato et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sato et al., 2008

claim: STAMBPL1 stabilizes XIAP to inhibit apoptosis in prostate cancer cells.
source: STAMBPL1 stabilizes XIAP to inhibit apoptosis in prostate cancer cells (Chen et al., 2019) and confers resistance to honokiol-induced apoptosis in various cancer cell types by stabilizing Survivin and c-FLIP (Woo et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2019

claim: STAMBPL1 confers resistance to honokiol-induced apoptosis in various cancer cell types by stabilizing Survivin and c-FLIP.
source: STAMBPL1 stabilizes XIAP to inhibit apoptosis in prostate cancer cells (Chen et al., 2019) and confers resistance to honokiol-induced apoptosis in various cancer cell types by stabilizing Survivin and c-FLIP (Woo et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Woo et al., 2019

claim: STAMBPL1 enhances cisplatin resistance in TNBC cells through the stabilization of MKP-1.
source: Our previous research demonstrated that STAMBPL1 enhances cisplatin resistance in TNBC cells through the stabilization of MKP-1 (Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2022

claim: STAMBPL1 upregulates HIF1α expression in TNBC cells independent of its deubiquitinating enzyme activity.
source: In this study, we discovered that, independent of its deubiquitinating enzyme activity, STAMBPL1 upregulates HIF1α expression in TNBC cells.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as a finding of the current study

claim: FOXO1 regulates various physiological and pathological processes, such as cell proliferation, apoptosis, autophagy, and oxidative stress.
source: FOXO1, a member of the forkhead box transcription factor family, regulates various physiological and pathological processes, such as cell proliferation, apoptosis, autophagy, and oxidative stress (Xing et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xing et al., 2018

claim: FOXO1 enhances the stemness of cancer cells by promoting SOX2 transcription in breast cancer.
source: In breast cancer, FOXO1 enhances the stemness of cancer cells by promoting SOX2 transcription (Yu et al., 2019) and confers resistance to chemotherapy drugs in basal-like breast cancer cells by activating KLF5 transcription (Cui et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yu et al., 2019

claim: FOXO1 confers resistance to chemotherapy drugs in basal-like breast cancer cells by activating KLF5 transcription.
source: In breast cancer, FOXO1 enhances the stemness of cancer cells by promoting SOX2 transcription (Yu et al., 2019) and confers resistance to chemotherapy drugs in basal-like breast cancer cells by activating KLF5 transcription (Cui et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cui et al., 2024

claim: FOXO1 plays a crucial role in angiogenesis by upregulating VEGFA transcription.
source: Furthermore, FOXO1 plays a crucial role in angiogenesis by upregulating VEGFA transcription (Jeon et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jeon et al., 2018

claim: STAMBPL1 facilitates the transcriptional regulation of GRHL3 by interacting with FOXO1.
source: In this study, we discovered that STAMBPL1 facilitates the transcriptional regulation of GRHL3 by interacting with FOXO1, consequently enhancing HIF1A transcription through GRHL3 to activate the HIF1α/VEGFA pathway.
evidence: Stated as a finding of the current study in the introduction

claim: STAMBPL1 enhances HIF1A transcription through GRHL3.
source: In this study, we discovered that STAMBPL1 facilitates the transcriptional regulation of GRHL3 by interacting with FOXO1, consequently enhancing HIF1A transcription through GRHL3 to activate the HIF1α/VEGFA pathway.
evidence: Stated as a finding of the current study in the introduction

claim: STAMBPL1 activates the HIF1α/VEGFA pathway to promote tumor angiogenesis in TNBC.
source: In this study, we discovered that STAMBPL1 facilitates the transcriptional regulation of GRHL3 by interacting with FOXO1, consequently enhancing HIF1A transcription through GRHL3 to activate the HIF1α/VEGFA pathway. This results in increased endothelial cell activity via paracrine signaling, thereby promoting tumor angiogenesis in TNBC.
evidence: Stated as a finding of the current study in the introduction

claim: Knockdown of STAMBPL1 inhibits hypoxia-induced HIF1α expression.
source: Western blot detected the protein levels of HIF1α when STAMBPL1 was knocked down under normoxia and hypoxia for 10 hr.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 1A

claim: Knockdown of STAMBPL1 suppresses the transcription of HIF1α downstream genes VEGFA and GLUT1.
source: To further investigate the role and mechanism of STAMBPL1 in TNBC, we discovered that the knockdown of STAMBPL1 can inhibit hypoxia-induced HIF1α expression (Figure 1A) and suppress the transcription of the HIF1α downstream genes VEGFA and GLUT1 (Figure 1B–E).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1B-E

claim: Both STAMBPL1 and its enzymatically mutated variant (E292A) can upregulate the protein expression of HIF1α under normoxic conditions.
source: Under normoxic conditions, both STAMBPL1 and its enzymatically mutated variant (E292A) can upregulate the protein expression of HIF1α (Figure 1F).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 1F

claim: STAMBPL1 enhances the expression of HIF1α in breast cancer cells through a non-DUB enzyme activity mechanism.
source: These findings suggest that STAMBPL1 enhances the expression of HIF1α in breast cancer cells through a non-DUB enzyme activity mechanism.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that the enzymatic mutant E292A also upregulates HIF1α

claim: Knocking down STAMBPL1 significantly inhibits the transcription of HIF1A under hypoxia.
source: To elucidate how STAMBPL1 upregulates HIF1α, we examined the transcription levels of HIF1A when STAMBPL1 was knocking down under hypoxia. These results indicate that knocking down STAMBPL1 significantly inhibits the transcription of HIF1A (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A-C

claim: STAMBPL1 overexpression increases the transcription of HIF1A under normoxia.
source: At the same time, we detected the transcription level of HIF1A and VEGFA when STAMBPL1 was overexpressing under normoxia. Data showed that STAMBPL1 overexpression increased the transcription of HIF1A (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E) and VEGFA (Figure 2E, G).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E

claim: STAMBPL1 overexpression increases the transcription of VEGFA under normoxia.
source: At the same time, we detected the transcription level of HIF1A and VEGFA when STAMBPL1 was overexpressing under normoxia. Data showed that STAMBPL1 overexpression increased the transcription of HIF1A (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E) and VEGFA (Figure 2E, G).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E, G

claim: The ability of STAMBPL1 to induce VEGFA transcription is blocked by HIF1α knockdown.
source: The ability of STAMBPL1 to induce VEGFA transcription was blocked by HIF1α knockdown (Figure 2D–G).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D-G

claim: STAMBPL1 activates the HIF1α/VEGFA axis through enhancing the transcription of HIF1A.
source: These findings suggested that STAMBPL1 activated the HIF1α/VEGFA axis through enhancing the transcription of HIF1A.
evidence: Inferred from the data showing STAMBPL1 increases HIF1A transcription and this effect is required for VEGFA induction

claim: Conditioned medium from TNBC cells with STAMBPL1 knockdown inhibits the proliferation of HUVECs.
source: The CM from TNBC cells with STAMBPL1 knockdown inhibited the proliferation (Figure 3A, B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B), migration (Figure 3C, D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D), and tube formation (Figure 3E, F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F) of HUVECs.
evidence: Demonstrated by EdU assay data shown in Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B

claim: Conditioned medium from TNBC cells with STAMBPL1 knockdown inhibits the migration of HUVECs.
source: The CM from TNBC cells with STAMBPL1 knockdown inhibited the proliferation (Figure 3A, B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B), migration (Figure 3C, D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D), and tube formation (Figure 3E, F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F) of HUVECs.
evidence: Demonstrated by wound healing assay data shown in Figure 3C, D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D

claim: Conditioned medium from TNBC cells with STAMBPL1 knockdown inhibits the tube formation of HUVECs.
source: The CM from TNBC cells with STAMBPL1 knockdown inhibited the proliferation (Figure 3A, B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B), migration (Figure 3C, D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D), and tube formation (Figure 3E, F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F) of HUVECs.
evidence: Demonstrated by tube formation assay data shown in Figure 3E, F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F

claim: STAMBPL1 overexpression in TNBC cells promotes the ability of HUVECs to proliferate, migrate, and form tubes, which can be reversed by knocking down HIF1α.
source: When STAMBPL1 was overexpressed in TNBC cells, the CM of HCC1806 and HCC1937 cells promoted the ability of HUVECs to proliferate (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, D), migrate (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, E), and form tubes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C, F), which could be reversed by knocking down HIF1α in TNBC cells.
evidence: Demonstrated by EdU, wound healing, and tube formation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-F

claim: STAMBPL1 activates the HIF1α/VEGFA axis in TNBC cells, leading to enhanced abilities of HUVECs through a paracrine pathway.
source: These findings suggest that STAMBPL1 activates the HIF1α/VEGFA axis in TNBC cells, leading to enhanced abilities of HUVECs through a paracrine pathway.
evidence: Inferred from the conditioned medium experiments showing STAMBPL1 effects on HUVECs are mediated through secreted factors

claim: Knocking down STAMBPL1 inhibits the growth of HCC1806 xenografts in mice.
source: Knocking down STAMBPL1 inhibited the growth of HCC1806 xenografts in mice (Figure 3G–I) and decreased the number of microvessels in tumor tissue (Figure 3J, K), indicating that STAMBPL1 promoted tumor angiogenesis.
evidence: Demonstrated by xenograft tumor growth data shown in Figure 3G-I

claim: Knocking down STAMBPL1 decreases the number of microvessels in tumor tissue.
source: Knocking down STAMBPL1 inhibited the growth of HCC1806 xenografts in mice (Figure 3G–I) and decreased the number of microvessels in tumor tissue (Figure 3J, K), indicating that STAMBPL1 promoted tumor angiogenesis.
evidence: Demonstrated by CD31 immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3J, K

claim: STAMBPL1 promotes tumor angiogenesis.
source: Knocking down STAMBPL1 inhibited the growth of HCC1806 xenografts in mice (Figure 3G–I) and decreased the number of microvessels in tumor tissue (Figure 3J, K), indicating that STAMBPL1 promoted tumor angiogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that STAMBPL1 knockdown reduces microvessel density in tumors

claim: Silencing of STAMBPL1 resulted in the downregulation of 27 genes (of which only 18 were annotated) in HCC1806 cells subjected to 10 hr of hypoxia.
source: By silencing the STAMBPL1 gene in HCC1806 cells subjected to 10 hr of hypoxia, we performed RNA-seq analysis to investigate the mechanism by which STAMBPL1 promotes HIF1A transcription. We found that silencing of STAMBPL1 resulted in the downregulation of 27 genes (of which only 18 were annotated).
evidence: Demonstrated by RNA-seq analysis results

claim: GRHL3 is a transcription factor involved in gene transcription regulation.
source: Of these 18 genes, except for GRHL3, which is a transcription factor reported to be involved in gene transcription regulation, the remaining 17 genes have no documented association with RNA transcription, stability, or modification (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Based on established knowledge about GRHL3 function

claim: Silencing of STAMBPL1 inhibits GRHL3 transcription in both HCC1806 and HCC1937 cells.
source: Silencing of STAMBPL1 inhibited GRHL3 transcription in both HCC1806 and HCC1937 cells (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B

claim: Overexpression of STAMBPL1 promotes GRHL3 transcription.
source: Conversely, the overexpression of STAMBPL1 promoted GRHL3 transcription (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D

claim: The stimulatory effects of STAMBPL1 on the HIF1α/VEGFA axis are reversed by GRHL3 knockdown.
source: Furthermore, the stimulatory effects of STAMBPL1 on the HIF1α/VEGFA axis (Figure 4C–F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–F) and on HUVECs (Figure 4G–I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1G–I) were reversed by GRHL3 knockdown.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C-F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-F

claim: The stimulatory effects of STAMBPL1 on HUVECs are reversed by GRHL3 knockdown.
source: Furthermore, the stimulatory effects of STAMBPL1 on the HIF1α/VEGFA axis (Figure 4C–F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–F) and on HUVECs (Figure 4G–I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1G–I) were reversed by GRHL3 knockdown.
evidence: Demonstrated by EdU, wound healing, and tube formation assay data shown in Figure 4G-I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1G-I

claim: STAMBPL1 activates the HIF1α/VEGFA axis by upregulating GRHL3.
source: These findings suggest that STAMBPL1 activates the HIF1α/VEGFA axis by upregulating GRHL3.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that GRHL3 knockdown reverses STAMBPL1 effects on HIF1α/VEGFA

claim: A GRHL-binding sequence was identified in the HIF1A promoter.
source: On the basis of the GRHL-binding motif (Figure 5A), a GRHL-binding sequence was identified in the HIF1A promoter (Figure 5B).
evidence: Based on bioinformatic analysis of the HIF1A promoter sequence shown in Figure 5A, B

claim: GRHL3 binds to the HIF1A promoter.
source: ChIP and luciferase assays revealed that GRHL3 bound to the HIF1A promoter (Figure 5D) and increased its activity (Figure 5E).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 5D

claim: GRHL3 increases the activity of the HIF1A promoter.
source: ChIP and luciferase assays revealed that GRHL3 bound to the HIF1A promoter (Figure 5D) and increased its activity (Figure 5E).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 5E

claim: Knockdown of GRHL3 results in decreased expression of HIF1α at both the mRNA and protein levels.
source: Knockdown of GRHL3 (Figure 5G, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) resulted in decreased expression of HIF1α at both the mRNA (Figure 5H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C) and protein levels (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), leading to suppressed VEGFA transcription (Figure 5I, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), indicating that GRHL3 promotes HIF1A transcription by binding to its promoter.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5F-H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C

claim: Knockdown of GRHL3 leads to suppressed VEGFA transcription.
source: Knockdown of GRHL3 (Figure 5G, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) resulted in decreased expression of HIF1α at both the mRNA (Figure 5H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C) and protein levels (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), leading to suppressed VEGFA transcription (Figure 5I, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), indicating that GRHL3 promotes HIF1A transcription by binding to its promoter.
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D

claim: GRHL3 promotes HIF1A transcription by binding to its promoter.
source: Knockdown of GRHL3 (Figure 5G, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) resulted in decreased expression of HIF1α at both the mRNA (Figure 5H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C) and protein levels (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), leading to suppressed VEGFA transcription (Figure 5I, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), indicating that GRHL3 promotes HIF1A transcription by binding to its promoter.
evidence: Inferred from the combined ChIP and knockdown data showing GRHL3 binds HIF1A promoter and regulates its expression

claim: Conditioned medium from TNBC cells with GRHL3 knockdown inhibits HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation.
source: Furthermore, CM from TNBC cells with GRHL3 knockdown inhibited HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation (Figure 5J–L, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: Demonstrated by EdU, wound healing, and tube formation assay data shown in Figure 5J-L and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E-G

claim: Overexpression of GRHL3 in TNBC cells activates the HIF1α/VEGFA axis.
source: The overexpression of GRHL3 in TNBC cells activated the HIF1α/VEGFA axis (Figure 6A, B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C), resulting in increased proliferation, migration, and tube formation in HUVECs.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6A, B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-C

claim: Overexpression of GRHL3 in TNBC cells results in increased proliferation, migration, and tube formation in HUVECs, which is reversed by knocking down HIF1α.
source: The overexpression of GRHL3 in TNBC cells activated the HIF1α/VEGFA axis (Figure 6A, B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C), resulting in increased proliferation, migration, and tube formation in HUVECs. This effect was reversed by knocking down HIF1α in TNBC cells (Figure 6C–E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: Demonstrated by EdU, wound healing, and tube formation assay data shown in Figure 6C-E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D, E

claim: Knockdown of GRHL3 inhibits tumor growth in HCC1806 xenograft mice.
source: Knockdown of GRHL3 (Figure 6F) also inhibited tumor growth in HCC1806 xenograft mice (Figure 6G–I) and reduced the number of microvessels in tumor tissues (Figure 6J, K).
evidence: Demonstrated by xenograft tumor growth data shown in Figure 6G-I

claim: Knockdown of GRHL3 reduces the number of microvessels in tumor tissues.
source: Knockdown of GRHL3 (Figure 6F) also inhibited tumor growth in HCC1806 xenograft mice (Figure 6G–I) and reduced the number of microvessels in tumor tissues (Figure 6J, K).
evidence: Demonstrated by CD31 immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6J, K

claim: STAMBPL1 is localized in the nucleus.
source: Our previous study demonstrated that STAMBPL1 is localized in the nucleus (Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2022

claim: FOXO1 acts as an upstream transcription factor of GRHL3.
source: Previous studies have indicated that FOXO1 acts as an upstream transcription factor of GRHL3 (Nagarajan et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nagarajan et al., 2017

claim: Knockdown of FOXO1 in TNBC cells inhibits the GRHL3/HIF1α/VEGFA axis.
source: Our experimental data revealed that knockdown of FOXO1 in TNBC cells not only inhibited the GRHL3/HIF1α/VEGFA axis (Figure 7A–D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–D) but also reversed the stimulatory effects of STAMBPL1 on this axis (Figure 7E–H).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7A-D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-D

claim: Knockdown of FOXO1 reverses the stimulatory effects of STAMBPL1 on the GRHL3/HIF1α/VEGFA axis.
source: Our experimental data revealed that knockdown of FOXO1 in TNBC cells not only inhibited the GRHL3/HIF1α/VEGFA axis (Figure 7A–D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–D) but also reversed the stimulatory effects of STAMBPL1 on this axis (Figure 7E–H).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7E-H

claim: FOXO1 binds to the promoter region of GRHL3.
source: Furthermore, FOXO1 was found to bind to the promoter region of GRHL3 (Figure 7I, Figure 7—figure supplement 1F) and enhance its transcriptional activity (Figure 7J).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 7I and Figure 7—figure supplement 1F

claim: FOXO1 enhances the transcriptional activity of GRHL3.
source: Furthermore, FOXO1 was found to bind to the promoter region of GRHL3 (Figure 7I, Figure 7—figure supplement 1F) and enhance its transcriptional activity (Figure 7J).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 7J

claim: STAMBPL1 increases the transcriptional activation of FOXO1 at the GRHL3 promoter.
source: STAMBPL1 was shown to increase the transcriptional activation of FOXO1 at the GRHL3 promoter (Figure 7K), and it also bound to the GRHL3 promoter which could be disrupted by FOXO1 knockdown (Figure 7L).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 7K

claim: STAMBPL1 binds to the GRHL3 promoter, which can be disrupted by FOXO1 knockdown.
source: STAMBPL1 was shown to increase the transcriptional activation of FOXO1 at the GRHL3 promoter (Figure 7K), and it also bound to the GRHL3 promoter which could be disrupted by FOXO1 knockdown (Figure 7L).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 7L

claim: Overexpression of STAMBPL1 and its enzymatic activity mutants does not affect the protein expression level of FOXO1.
source: However, the overexpression of STAMBPL1 and its enzymatic activity mutants did not affect the protein expression level of FOXO1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E

claim: STAMBPL1 and FOXO1 colocalize in the nucleus.
source: We observed the colocalization of STAMBPL1 and FOXO1 in the nucleus (Figure 7M) and identified an interaction between them in HCC1937 cells (Figure 7N).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7M

claim: STAMBPL1 interacts with FOXO1 in HCC1937 cells.
source: We observed the colocalization of STAMBPL1 and FOXO1 in the nucleus (Figure 7M) and identified an interaction between them in HCC1937 cells (Figure 7N).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7N

claim: The N-terminus (1–140 aa) of STAMBPL1 interacts with FOXO1.
source: The results of the GST pull-down assay indicated that the N-terminus (1–140 aa) of STAMBPL1 interacted with FOXO1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: Demonstrated by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1I

claim: The FOXO1 protein (250–596 aa) interacts with STAMBPL1.
source: Additionally, an immunoprecipitation assay revealed an interaction between the FOXO1 protein (250–596 aa) and STAMBPL1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1J

claim: STAMBPL1 promotes GRHL3 transcription by interacting with FOXO1.
source: These findings suggest that STAMBPL1 promotes GRHL3 transcription by interacting with FOXO1.
evidence: Inferred from the combined data showing STAMBPL1-FOXO1 interaction and their cooperative effects on GRHL3 transcription

claim: The expression levels of STAMBPL1, FOXO1, and GRHL3 in TNBC are significantly higher than those in non-TNBC.
source: Through an analysis of the Metabric database in BCIP (http://www.omicsnet.org/bcancer), it was observed that while the expression levels of STAMBPL1, FOXO1, and GRHL3 in breast cancer tissues are not universally elevated compared to adjacent non-cancerous tissues, but their expression levels in TNBC are significantly higher than those in non-TNBC (Figure 8A–C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Demonstrated by Metabric database analysis shown in Figure 8A-C and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A-C

claim: STAMBPL1 overexpression enhances breast cancer cell growth in vivo.
source: Our findings indicated that STAMBPL1 overexpression enhanced breast cancer cell growth in vivo.
evidence: Demonstrated by xenograft tumor growth experiments

claim: The individual inhibitory effects of the FOXO1 and VEGFR inhibitors on tumor growth are not significant.
source: While the individual inhibitory effects of the FOXO1 and VEGFR inhibitors on tumor growth were not significant, the combined treatment markedly suppressed tumor growth in nude mice (Figure 8E–G).
evidence: Demonstrated by xenograft tumor growth data shown in Figure 8E-G

claim: The combined treatment of FOXO1 inhibitor AS1842856 and VEGFR inhibitor apatinib markedly suppresses tumor growth in nude mice.
source: While the individual inhibitory effects of the FOXO1 and VEGFR inhibitors on tumor growth were not significant, the combined treatment markedly suppressed tumor growth in nude mice (Figure 8E–G).
evidence: Demonstrated by xenograft tumor growth data shown in Figure 8E-G

claim: The drug treatments (AS1842856 and apatinib) do not affect the body weights of the mice.
source: Importantly, the drug treatments did not affect the body weights of the mice (Figure 8H).
evidence: Demonstrated by body weight measurements shown in Figure 8H

claim: The combined administration of AS1842856 and apatinib effectively inhibits tumor growth in nude mice.
source: These results suggest that the combined administration of AS1842856 and apatinib effectively inhibits tumor growth in nude mice.
evidence: Inferred from the xenograft data showing synergistic effects of combined treatment

claim: STAMBPL1 promotes angiogenesis in TNBC by activating the HIF1α/VEGFA pathway independently of its enzymatic activity.
source: In this study, we discovered that STAMBPL1 promotes angiogenesis in TNBC by activating the HIF1α/VEGFA pathway independently of its enzymatic activity.
evidence: Stated as a main finding in the Discussion section

claim: STAMBPL1 positively regulates the transcription of GRHL3.
source: Through RNA-seq analysis, we revealed that STAMBPL1 positively regulates the transcription of GRHL3.
evidence: Demonstrated by RNA-seq analysis

claim: GRHL3 binds to the promoter of the HIF1A gene, thereby increasing its transcription.
source: Furthermore, we demonstrated that GRHL3 binds to the promoter of the HIF1A gene, thereby increasing its transcription.
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP and luciferase assays

claim: STAMBPL1 interacts with FOXO1 to facilitate the transcription of GRHL3/HIF1α/VEGFA.
source: Additionally, we found that STAMBPL1 interacts with FOXO1 to facilitate the transcription of GRHL3/HIF1α/VEGFA.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation and functional assays

claim: The combination of the FOXO1 inhibitor AS1842856 and the VEGFR inhibitor apatinib effectively inhibits tumor growth in nude mice.
source: Importantly, we confirmed that the combination of the FOXO1 inhibitor AS1842856 and the VEGFR inhibitor apatinib effectively inhibited tumor growth in nude mice.
evidence: Demonstrated by xenograft experiments

claim: Both STAMBPL1 and FOXO1 may be potential therapeutic targets for inhibiting angiogenesis in TNBC.
source: These findings suggest that both STAMBPL1 and FOXO1 may be potential therapeutic targets for inhibiting angiogenesis in TNBC.
evidence: Inferred from the combined findings showing their roles in TNBC angiogenesis and the efficacy of FOXO1 inhibition

claim: This study is the first to uncover the role of STAMBPL1 in promoting angiogenesis through the FOXO1/GRHL3/HIF1α axis.
source: This study is the first to uncover the role of STAMBPL1 in promoting angiogenesis through the FOXO1/GRHL3/HIF1α axis.
evidence: Stated as a novel finding in the Discussion section

claim: GRHL3 is a novel transcription factor that regulates the transcription of HIF1α.
source: Furthermore, a novel transcription factor, GRHL3, which regulates the transcription of HIF1α was identified.
evidence: Stated as a novel finding in the Discussion section

claim: STAMBPL1 has been reported to be involved in the epithelial‒mesenchymal transition of various cancers.
source: Recent studies have reported its involvement in the epithelial‒mesenchymal transition of various cancers, and its absence has been shown to affect the mesenchymal phenotype of lung and breast cancer (Ambroise et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ambroise et al., 2020

claim: The absence of STAMBPL1 affects the mesenchymal phenotype of lung and breast cancer.
source: Recent studies have reported its involvement in the epithelial‒mesenchymal transition of various cancers, and its absence has been shown to affect the mesenchymal phenotype of lung and breast cancer (Ambroise et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ambroise et al., 2020

claim: The deletion of STAMBPL1 and MKP1 increases the sensitivity of breast cancer cells to cisplatin.
source: Our previous research demonstrated that STAMBPL1 can stabilize MKP1 through deubiquitination and that the deletion of STAMBPL1 and MKP1 increases the sensitivity of breast cancer cells to cisplatin (Liu et al., 2022), suggesting that STAMBPL1 may be a potential therapeutic target for breast cancer.
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2022

claim: STAMBPL1 may be a potential therapeutic target for breast cancer.
